title: Own and close the core event lifecycle
working_tree_status: dirty shared worktree; control-plane-only task creation
goal: Adopt the remaining event, calendar, status, and hold actions and make their authorization contract explicit.

in: Adopt the remaining event, calendar, status, and hold actions and make their authorization contract explicit.

working_set_additions.reason: Code evidence: events_v2 has SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE policies from 20250816133000_event_core.sql but no DELETE policy in any migration, so the event delete action had no data-boundary authorization at all. Additive, idempotent, manual-apply only (CP-051). Not applied by this lane.

resume_condition: An operator applies 20260927110000_events_v2_delete_rls.sql under CP-051, then npx vitest run __tests__/events/ confirms the delete action is live at the data boundary. Every other criterion is local and met; resume the lane only for that apply and its postflight.

blocked_on.condition: Operator action, not a task dependency: apply supabase/migrations/20260927110000_events_v2_delete_rls.sql to an approved staging or production target under CP-051 (explicitly, one at a time; no db reset, no forced replay), then rerun npx vitest run __tests__/events/ to confirm the delete action is live at the data boundary. No agent can perform this: CP-051 forbids an automated apply and no target has been provisioned. No other acceptance criterion in this task is outstanding.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Adopt the remaining event, calendar, status, and hold actions and make their authorization contract explicit.
evidence: lib/events/event-lifecycle-service.ts is the single owner of create, update, delete, status transition, org calendar, hold, and event calendar items, with the authorization contract stated in its module header.

Rules: event.manage on the owning org; org resolved server-side from the resource; a client tourId may select but never grant an org; every write bound by both resource id and authorized org_id; request-scoped RLS client only, never service role.
app/api/events/route.ts POST, app/api/events/[id]/route.ts PATCH/DELETE/GET, app/api/events/[id]/hq/calendar/route.ts, and app/events/_actions/event-actions.ts are now thin shells over that service.
npx vitest run __tests__/events/ -> 16 files, 127 tests passed.
Same route suite against base SHA 16fb834f in an isolated worktree -> 11 of 12 failed, including cross-tenant create via a foreign tour_id returning 200 and unbound PATCH/DELETE writes.

Open gap, not yet live: the delete action's data-boundary gate depends on the unapplied migration 20260927110000_events_v2_delete_rls.sql. Code and denial tests are in place; the allow path cannot succeed in a real database until the database lane applies it. That is why this task stays active rather than completed.

progress.summary: BLOCKED, not idle-by-choice (orchestrator, Wave 37, 2026-09-28). The working set was narrowed from app/api/events/** to the seven files this task owns so the 26 sub-resource route files could go to EVENTS-004 without a collision. Its only remaining step is an operator apply it cannot perform; the malformed blocker it carried (type undefined, empty condition) has been replaced with a real one.
completed: Adopted create, update, delete, status transition, org calendar, hold, and event calendar item actions into lib/events/event-lifecycle-service.ts as the single owner with explicit inputs

Made the authorization contract explicit: event.manage on the owning org, server-resolved org, tourId may select but never grant an org, every write bound by resource id plus authorized org_id, request-scoped RLS client only

Reduced app/api/events/route.ts, app/api/events/[id]/route.ts, app/api/events/[id]/hq/calendar/route.ts, and app/events/_actions/event-actions.ts to thin shells with no inline authorization or state mutation
Closed cross-tenant event creation via a client-supplied tour_id (was HTTP 200 at base SHA) and cross-org tour attachment
Removed the service-role client from the event HQ calendar action and replaced the handler-only permission check with the shared contract
Fixed a latent bug where the HQ calendar route derived the event id from path segment -2, which resolved to 'hq' instead of the event id
Gated ensureAdminOrgScope against self-granting an owner membership in an org named only by a client tourId
Wrote additive idempotent migration 20260927110000_events_v2_delete_rls.sql adding the missing events_v2 DELETE policy; manual-apply only, not applied
Added 39 denial and authorization tests across __tests__/events/event-lifecycle-authorization.test.ts and __tests__/events/event-routes-authorization.test.ts
next_steps: Database lane applies supabase/migrations/20260927110000_events_v2_delete_rls.sql to the target environment via supabase migration up or targeted psql (CP-051, no db reset)
After apply, re-run npx vitest run __tests__/events/ and confirm the delete action is live at the data boundary, then close EVENTS-001

Open a follow-up events task for the sub-resource routes under app/api/events/[id]/ (staff, vendors, tasks, jobs, incidents, participants, locations, group-chats, posts, share-message, hq/resources, hq/permissions), which are outside this task's core lifecycle scope and were not audited

ORCHESTRATOR NARROW (Wave 37, 2026-09-28): the broad app/api/events/** and __tests__/events/** claims were narrowed to the files this task actually owns, because EVENTS-004 needs the 26 sub-resource route files and the two tasks collided in the control plane. event-routes-authorization.test.ts transferred to EVENTS-004: the only sub-resource route it exercises is [id]/hq/calendar, which is in that grant. Nothing about this task acceptance changes, and its blocker is still the database apply.
Report to the database lane that venues_v2 and venue_profiles carry no org_id, so an event cannot be bound to an org-owned venue; the contract only requires the venue to exist
